title: node.json
description: Knowledge nodes (contracts.md §2.3). `knowledgeKind` is authored, never derived: `metis` marks knowledge that codification destroys, and it is a content judgement rather than a function of tier or cell (see docs/design/metis-authoring.md). Every cost is fixed-point at scale 1024. `rediscoveryMultiplier` carries a content invariant of >= fp(3072); v1 authors at >= fp(5376) so species rediscoveryAffinity has room to differentiate above the floor. fp(4096) is explicitly not enough — the best v1 affinity drives it under the floor and clamps the trait flat. The authoring floor is a graph-phase check in load.ts, not a schema minimum, because it is a function of species affinity rather than of the field alone. load.ts also rejects a researchCost whose rediscovery requirement overflows fixed point at the worst species affinity, which these maxima alone permit. `magnitude` is signed: a negative one is a COST, and it is what lets a node express the other half of a tradeoff instead of degenerating into a bonus. The sign rule is a graph-phase check in load.ts rather than a schema minimum, because whether a negative is meaningful depends on the stacking rule primitive.json declares — permitted for `additive-into-multiplier` and refused for every other rule (contracts.md §3). Zero is refused there too, since this interpreter implements neither `not` nor `exclusiveMinimum`.

antirequisites.description: Nodes this one may never be held alongside, **in one mind**. The inverse of `prerequisites`, and the first irreversible choice in the game: a prerequisite graph is a partial order, so a long enough life climbs all of it, while an exclusion makes two repertoires mutually unreachable and two mages genuinely incomparable. Declared on one side and enforced on both — load.ts normalises the relation, so holding either member blocks the other whichever arrived first. Scoped to the mage rather than the universe because vision.md §5 puts a knowledge instance in exactly one mind: a universe may still hold both lines, at the price of spending two different mages on them.

gradeRequirement.description: This one effect contributes only while the universe holds refined material, and consumes that material while it does. Absent means unconditional, which is what every effect authored before grades existed means and must go on meaning. It is per **effect** rather than per node on purpose: `cig-the-standing-furnace` runs the great foundries on ore and also denies a field to anyone walking through one, and gating the second on a quarry would be a raid effect switched off by an economy. Semantics are `economy-flow-models.md` §1.1's **gate**, not its drain: short, and the effect contributes nothing that tick and nothing is destroyed.

revealTarget.description: What a `reveal` effect makes audible. At least one of the two; both means the conjunction — a latent effect matches only when its cell and its primitive both match.

control.description: Rego's gate (sound-design.md §4.1: 'Snap, lock, gate'). A floor is reliability bought; a ceiling is upside sold. At least one. Both are fp bounds on the primitive's stacked outcome, applied after the fold and before the primitive's own cap, so control may never lift a value past contracts.md §3's cap.
